requirements.requirement: Existing /srv/inventory data is owned by inventorysvc and accessible to inventory-readers while inaccessible to other users.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart observations show inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership throughout, directory mode 0750, file mode 0640, no other-user permission bits, successful reader-group access, and denial for an unrelated user.
The same two files remain, and their SHA-256 hashes match the preparation baseline before repair, after repair, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 are identical before and after execution. The repair used existing RHEL 7 system utilities and did not install or replace software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, a different boot ID was observed, and SSH, identities, permissions, checksums, and access controls recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition. Hygiene is strong aside from three minor abandoned /tmp files.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency was not independently established.
The lifecycle collector did not independently probe /srv/inventory; task-state conclusions rely on coherent executor command observations plus the authored preparation baseline.
Three executor-created temporary evidence files remained under /tmp after completion.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating the required identities, repairing ownership/modes, testing access, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. The initial unprivileged repair attempt made no observed changes because identity creation, chown, and chmod all failed. Three small evidence/restart artifacts were unnecessarily left in /tmp: inventory-other.err, inventory-reboot.log, and inventory-other-post.err; they remained at final collection. No failed services or new listening endpoints were observed.
